findings.text: the only gate log recorded for the repair names revision 6494baff, whose tests/test_fleet_supervisor.py carries six cases and whose fleet_supervisor.py has neither the settle rule nor _set_pty_size, while the same log reports 8 passed; the tree measured was the uncommitted repair, so the log's revision line and its own result contradict each other, nothing can be replayed at the revision it names, and no gate log exists at the reviewed head (my own re-run there is 8 passed, at the run directory's recheck-gate.log).

item_verdicts.diff: the two repair commits read against 6494baff — 4f7dacd2 rewrites the tab wait as a settle window, adds the pty set-and-read-back and the detach exit status in reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py, and adds the corresponding cases; ce399498 corrects the quoted timestamp and records the measurement gaps in the two doc pages; no plan state scalar is mutated.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when names tests/test_fleet_supervisor.py, an on-node check with the real 0.45.1 binary and an executed negative control; the gate file carries 8 cases with the create-attach-query ordering assertion that reddens under the declared mutation, the size read back from the kernel and the client's own exit status, and the on-node log records four tabs with no pane error under a whole-log positive control over the same instrument; my own re-run at ce399498 is 8 passed.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is a headless fleet session that keeps every layout tab when its first client attaches; reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py:344 attaches a 200x50 pty client for the layout and holds it until the tab list has been non-empty and unchanged for 2.5 s (fleet_supervisor.py:294) before detaching at :341, so at the ~1.5 s cadence the recording shows the client outlives every tab, with the residual that a window rather than the layout's declared tab count decides when the layout is done.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records the two repair commits, names the gate and the on-node log, lists the three review-requested controls with their logs, and states honestly in follow_ons that the defect did not reproduce in the node's own probes — but the gate log it cites names a revision at which the content that log measured does not exist.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the diff 0260fc7b..ce399498 touches five paths (reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py, tests/test_fleet_supervisor.py, docs/evidence/archive/a-dispatch-returns-without-its-worker-landed.html, docs/figures/a-dispatch-returns-without-its-worker/headless_tab_sizing.svg, docs/plans/a-dispatch-returns-without-its-worker.html), all inside the declared write paths, the worktree is clean at ce399498, and the repair's plan-page edit adds a paragraph without touching a plan meta scalar.

justifications.durability: each of the three properties the prior review found unmeasured is now asserted against a source the code cannot compose — the kernel read-back at tests/test_fleet_supervisor.py:536, the client's own exit status at :492 and the slow layout's full list at :516 — with an executed control behind each, and the residual is that the slow case's 0.3 s spacing is faster than the recorded 1.5 s cadence, so it pins the rule rather than the constant's fit, and a wait that ended only at its 20 s bound would also pass it.
justifications.evidence: the three controls are logged with their scratch module paths and their intended assertions (negative_control_wait.log, negative_control_pty_size.log, negative_control_detach.log), the corrected excerpt's timestamps all match the source log it quotes, and my own re-run of the gate at the reviewed head is 8 passed — but the gate log the manifest cites names 6494baff, a revision that does not carry the content that log measured.
justifications.fit: the repaired helpers follow the module's log()/constant idiom and are named by mechanism (TAB_SETTLE_SECONDS, _set_pty_size, _detach_client), no plan label enters code or comments, and the one upstream identifier at fleet_supervisor.py:81 is the removal condition the node's done_when names.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py:344 attaches the fixed-size client and holds it until the settle window at :294 has seen the tab list quiet for 2.5 s before detaching at :341, so the client now outlives the tab spacing the recording shows, and the residual is that the window rather than the layout's declared tab count decides when the layout is done.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path of 0260fc7b..ce399498 lies inside the declared write paths, the worktree is clean at ce399498, and the repair's plan-page edit adds a paragraph without mutating a plan meta scalar.
